_comment: DECLARATIVE KWin window rules — data-driven, consumed by window-rules.nix. Rules are applied with kwriteconfig6 at activation rather than by owning ~/.config/kwinrulesrc outright: KWin REWRITES that file whenever a rule is edited in System Settings, so a /nix/store symlink there would be replaced by a real file on first GUI edit and the declaration would silently stop applying — the exact failure konsolerc, Profile 1.profile and baloofilerc all hit (see app_especific/konsole.nix). Setting individual keys instead re-asserts ours on every switch while leaving any rule the user adds by hand untouched.
_desktop_ids_doc: KWin identifies virtual desktops by the Id_N strings in ~/.config/kwinrc [Desktops], NOT by position. This machine: Id_1=Desktop_1 (Desk1) … Id_4=Desktop_4 (Desk4). Plasma 6 dropped kstart's --desktop flag (kstart 6.2.5 has only --desktopfile/--application), so launching a window onto a specific desktop is no longer possible from the command line — a window rule is the supported mechanism.
_desktopsrule_doc: KWin rule 'set' modes: 1=Apply Initially, 2=Force, 3=Remember, 4=Apply Now, 5=Force Temporarily. Force (2) is used so the window cannot drift to whichever desktop happened to be active when the build started.

rules._comment: THREE windows, one rule. build.sh opens a Konsole via its own konsole_wrap AND flakes-switch-progress-logs opens another, and switch-progress.sh adds a kdialog — all three used to land on whatever desktop was focused, burying the work in progress. Desk3 is deliberate: default-session.json leaves desktop 3 empty (1=konsole+my-konsole, 2=brave, 4=dolphin+kate), so builds get a dedicated space and never cover the terminal that launched them.
